name: sendmmsg
synopsis: int sendmmsg(int sockfd, struct mmsghdr *msgvec, unsigned int vlen, int flags);
description: The sendmmsg() system call is an extension of sendmsg(2) that allows transmitting multiple messages on a socket using a single system call, providing performance benefits for some applications. It operates on a socket file descriptor and an array of message headers.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the socket on which data is to be transmitted.

parameters.name: msgvec
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of mmsghdr structures, each containing a msghdr and a field for bytes transmitted.

parameters.name: vlen
parameters.description: Size of the array pointed to by msgvec, capped at UIO_MAXIOV (1024).

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags ORed together, identical to those used in sendmsg(2).

return_value.success: Returns the number of messages sent from msgvec; if less than vlen, the caller can retry.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error.

errors.description: Various errors as described in sendmsg(2); an error is returned only if no datagrams could be sent.

bugs: If an error occurs after at least one message has been sent, the call succeeds and returns the number of messages sent, but the error code is lost; the caller must retry starting from the first failed message, with no guarantee of the same error.
